stories.headline: DOJ sues Denver over ICE mask ban; Mayor Johnston vows to fight federal lawsuit
stories.summary:
The U.S. Department of Justice filed suit Thursday in U.S. District Court of Colorado against the City of Denver, Mayor Mike Johnston, City Attorney Miko Brown, and Police Chief Ron Thomas over a city ordinance banning federal immigration agents from wearing face coverings while on duty in Denver. The ordinance, signed into law earlier this year, also requires federal officers to display visible identification and allows Denver police to cite non-complying agents with fines up to $999 and up to 300 days in jail.

The DOJ lawsuit argues the ordinance violates the Supremacy Clause of the U.S. Constitution, asserting that complying with the local law would endanger federal officers by exposing their identities to the public, potentially enabling harassment by organized crime or transnational criminal organizations. The complaint claims families of two federal agents in the Denver metro area and Durango have already been doxxed and harassed after their images were posted online.

Mayor Johnston responded shortly after the city was served, vowing to 'fight to the very end' to uphold the ordinance. Johnston said law enforcement officers operating in Denver should be transparent and accountable, identifiable by badge, name, and badge number. The DOJ is asking the court to declare the ordinance invalid as applied to federal officers and to permanently block the city from enforcing it.

stories.headline: Denver grand jury indicts 12 people in elaborate luxury car theft scheme tied to predatory towing operations
stories.summary:
A Denver grand jury last month indicted 12 individuals on 187 counts including motor vehicle theft, forgery, and defrauding creditors, insurance companies, and the government in connection with a multistate scheme to steal Lamborghinis and other high-end vehicles through predatory towing operations. Investigators say the enterprise used tow truck drivers to solicit business at crash scenes under false pretenses, then charged exorbitant storage fees to coerce owners into abandoning their vehicles.

The group allegedly sold stolen vehicles for more than $2.5 million in total, often wrapping cars in film, changing their colors, and adding custom wheels to conceal their identities. Defendants also targeted car owners behind on loan payments, posing as bank representatives, forging Colorado DMV documents to obtain fraudulent titles, and selling the vehicles to unsuspecting buyers.

The investigation was overseen by the Denver District Attorney's Office and led by the Colorado Metropolitan Auto Theft Task Force, with assistance from the state Division of Motor Vehicles, the Colorado Public Utilities Commission, and the National Insurance Crime Bureau. Denver District Attorney John Walsh described the operation as a 'multi-year criminal enterprise' that exploited both accident victims and financially distressed vehicle owners.

stories.headline: GOP-led House Judiciary Committee report charges Colorado sanctuary policies threaten public safety
stories.summary:
A report released Thursday by the Republican-led U.S. House Judiciary Committee, chaired by Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio, argues that Colorado's sanctuary policies — particularly those in Denver and Boulder — undermine federal immigration enforcement and endanger public safety. The 24-page interim staff report specifically criticizes Denver District Attorney John Walsh and Boulder District Attorney Michael Dougherty for factoring immigration consequences into charging decisions and plea agreements.

The committee previously subpoenaed Dougherty on Sept. 16, demanding records by Sept. 25, and alleges he failed to produce a single document in response to requests made more than three months ago. The report calls for Congress to pass the 'Shutdown Sanctuary Policies Act,' which would prohibit local restrictions on cooperation with federal immigration authorities.

Dougherty dismissed the report as a political stunt timed ahead of the November midterm elections. 'My responsibility is to do justice, enhance public safety, and fight for victims,' Dougherty said in an emailed statement. Colorado officials and their Democratic allies have argued that local governments should not be compelled to redirect their resources to assist federal immigration enforcement.

stories.headline: Avalanche beat Flames 7-3, erupting for 23 goals in first four games of season
stories.summary:
The Colorado Avalanche defeated the Calgary Flames 7-3 Thursday night, with Cale Makar recording two goals and an assist, and Devon Toews and Jaden Schwartz each scoring twice. The victory extended Colorado's hot start to the 2026-27 NHL season and followed a 3-2 road loss to the Winnipeg Jets on Wednesday.

The Avalanche have now scored 23 goals across their first four games, a pace that has not been matched in more than 30 years, according to reporting aggregated by the Denver Post. The offensive outburst has put the rest of the NHL on notice as Colorado looks to contend for a championship this season.

Head coach Jared Bednar addressed media after the Flames win, speaking to the team's offensive depth beyond top stars. The Avalanche's schedule continues with further road and home games as they look to build on their 3-1 start.

stories.headline: Broncos place wide receiver Pat Bryant on injured reserve; starting corners Surtain, Moss ruled out vs. Chargers
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos placed second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant on injured reserve Friday due to the ankle injury he sustained in Sunday's loss to San Francisco, sidelining him for a minimum of four games. Bryant had nine catches for 133 yards and a touchdown on the season before going down. Head coach Sean Payton had said earlier in the week he did not expect Bryant to land on IR.

The team also ruled out both starting cornerbacks Pat Surtain II (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) for Sunday's Week 5 game at home against the Los Angeles Chargers. Second-year corner Jahdae Barron and third-year corner Kris Abrams-Draine will start in their place, with undrafted rookie Brent Austin expected to be elevated from the practice squad.

To replace Bryant at receiver, the Broncos promoted Lil'Jordan Humphrey back to the 53-man roster. The Chargers will also be shorthanded Sunday, ruled out seven players including star safety Derwin James and placed tackle Rashawn Slater on injured reserve earlier in the week.

stories.headline: Denver metro home sales fall to weakest September since 2008 financial crisis as mortgage rates hit 7.5%
stories.summary:
Metro Denver closed sales dropped to 2,849 in September, a 12% decline from August and a 21% decline from September 2025, marking the weakest September performance in records going back to the height of the 2008 recession, according to the Denver Metro Association of Realtors' monthly report. The slowdown coincides with the 30-year fixed mortgage rate climbing every week through September, peaking near 7.5%, and the Federal Reserve raising its benchmark rate for the first time since July 2023.

Most September closings went under contract in August when rates hovered around 6.7%, meaning the full effect of the rate spike may not appear until October and November closings are tallied. Year-to-date closings trail 2025 by 5%, a gap that continues to widen. Pending sales slipped 6% to 2,908, signaling a soft but not panicked buyer response to higher borrowing costs.

Despite the sales slowdown, median prices for detached homes have held steady, with the year-to-date median close price at $650,000 — matching each of the past two years. The metro ended September with 13,567 active listings and 4.76 months of inventory, giving buyers more negotiating leverage. The luxury segment above $1 million bucked the broader trend, with year-to-date sales rising 2% and a median of just 21 days on market, compared to 32 days metro-wide.

stories.headline: Gov. Polis signs executive order to lower gas and grocery prices amid war-driven fuel spike
stories.summary:
Colorado Gov. Jared Polis signed an executive order Friday temporarily modifying select environmental and transportation policies aimed at reducing gas prices for state residents, citing the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict as the driver of fuel costs. Gas prices in Colorado have risen above $4 per gallon, with diesel exceeding $6 per gallon.

Details of the specific policy modifications included in the order were not fully disclosed in initial reporting, but the action reflects the governor's effort to provide short-term relief to consumers facing higher costs at the pump and grocery store. The executive action is described as temporary in nature.

The move adds to Polis's recent executive activity, which has included appointing a special envoy to address a longstanding land dispute involving a family with a state Supreme Court-affirmed inherited easement. Polis said of that separate matter, 'The status quo is this thing could be in litigation for many more decades, or we could try to find a better way.'

stories.headline: 3-year-old girl and 43-year-old man identified as victims of Boulder County plane crash near Eldorado Springs
stories.summary:
The Boulder County Coroner's Office has identified the two victims killed in a plane crash near Eldorado Springs as Aaron Gingrich, 43, and a 3-year-old girl. The crash occurred in Boulder County, and investigators have been working to determine the cause.

The identification of the victims was announced Thursday by Fox31 Denver, citing the coroner's office. No additional details about the circumstances of the crash or the relationship between the victims had been released at time of publication.

The National Transportation Safety Board typically investigates small aircraft crashes of this nature, though no federal agency statements were included in initial reports. Eldorado Springs is located in the foothills southwest of Boulder.

stories.headline: Two people hospitalized after shooting on Stout Street in downtown Denver
stories.summary:
Denver police are investigating a Thursday night shooting in the 2100 block of Stout Street that left two victims with what appeared to be non-life-threatening injuries. Both individuals were transported to a hospital, and officers were working to develop suspect information as of early Friday.

No details about what led to the shooting had been released by the Denver Police Department at the time of initial reporting. The investigation remained ongoing, with no suspect information publicly disclosed.

The Stout Street corridor runs through a busy section of downtown Denver near several residential and commercial blocks. DPD has not released descriptions of any suspects or indicated whether the shooting was targeted or random.

stories.headline: September rains from Hurricane Polo shrink Colorado drought footprint, but relief remains incomplete
stories.summary:
Heavy rainfall driven by Hurricane Polo in September significantly reduced Colorado's drought profile, particularly in the southern half of the state, according to reports from the Colorado Climate Center at Colorado State University and the U.S. Drought Monitor. The share of Colorado completely free of drought rose from 8.94% to 15.62% in a single week, and is up from just 1.68% three months ago.

The Colorado Climate Center reported that some spots in southwestern and southeastern Colorado recorded their wettest September on record, with most of the southern half of the state receiving more than twice normal precipitation. That resulted in one- to two-category drought improvements in the weekly federal monitor. Northern Colorado fared worse, with some Front Range locations receiving less than half their typical September precipitation.

State Climatologist Russ Schumacher cautioned that the improvements do not mean the drought is resolved. Reservoirs in southwest Colorado remain in poor condition, and ranchers and farmers who rely on irrigation did not receive adequate water when they needed it. The worst drought conditions persist in the central Colorado high country, including parts of Routt, Grand, Eagle, Pitkin, and Chaffee counties, as well as portions of Larimer, Boulder, Weld, and El Paso counties.

stories.headline: Denver Zoo rhino Rupert dies after months of gastrointestinal illness; second rhino death at zoo this year
stories.summary:
Rupert, a 12-year-old greater one-horned rhinoceros, died Saturday at the Denver Zoo Conservation Alliance after a months-long battle with recurring gastrointestinal illness, zoo officials announced Thursday. Rupert had arrived from a San Diego zoo in May under a Species Survival Plan recommendation that he breed with the zoo's 18-year-old female rhino, Tensing, but the two were never formally introduced.

His care team began managing symptoms about a month after his arrival, in June, and he underwent multiple treatments including procedures under standing sedation. His condition declined significantly over the weekend before his death, and he was surrounded by caretakers at the time.

Rupert's death is the second rhino loss at the Denver Zoo in 2026. Rudisha, a beloved 32-year-old black rhino, died in May after entering end-of-life care for age-related mobility challenges. Zoo officials said Rupert's illness is considered an individual case and that Tensing's health is not a concern.

stories.headline: Veo launches multi-year plan to reduce sidewalk scooter riding in Denver with new detection technology and escalating fines
stories.summary:
Veo, Denver's exclusive shared scooter and bike operator since May, announced a multi-year Safe Sidewalks Plan Thursday aimed at curbing prohibited sidewalk riding through expanded detection technology, escalating rider fines, and education campaigns. Every Veo vehicle already carries location-based detection that triggers audible warnings when sidewalk riding is detected downtown, and the company is testing laser sensors as a secondary system, with both technologies targeted for the full fleet by September 2027.

Since activating in-ride warnings in July, Veo reports sidewalk riding downtown has dropped about 10%, with more than 2,600 warnings issued to date. Under Denver's ordinance effective July 1, enforcement responsibility for sidewalk riding shifts to the operator, and repeated violations under Veo's escalating system can result in fines and account suspensions.

Veo reported 1.34 million rides in its first two months operating Denver's program, a 12% increase from the same period under previous operators, with more than 42% of rides coming through its Access program for income-qualified riders. The plan also calls for 40 new designated parking corrals near Union Station by year's end and continued outreach by sidewalk ambassadors. Denver rules permit sidewalk use only to begin or end a trip on the same block, and only at 6 mph or slower.

topStory.headline: Trump Announces Russia-U.S. Diesel Deal with Putin, Eases Sanctions as Ukraine War Escalates
topStory.summary:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to release millions of tonnes of diesel fuel onto global markets following a phone call between the two leaders. According to Trump's post on Truth Social, Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November, 1 million tonnes shortly thereafter, and an additional 3 million tonnes within a short period. The Treasury Department simultaneously issued a temporary general license through the Office of Foreign Assets Control authorizing the sale, delivery, and importation of Russian-origin diesel fuel into the United States and global markets through April 7, 2027.

The Kremlin confirmed the call lasted approximately one and a half hours and covered large-scale economic initiatives, including Russian fuel supplies. Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev praised the agreement on X, writing that 'Russia-U.S. cooperation on diesel and energy will benefit the world.' Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told state news agency TASS that Russia would immediately begin lifting its diesel export ban, which had been in place since July and extended through the end of October, as a direct result of the Trump-Putin agreement.

The deal comes against the backdrop of sharply elevated diesel prices, which have risen nearly 70 percent since the start of the Iran war in February, with the national average standing at $6.27 per gallon according to the American Automobile Association. Ukrainian air strikes on Russian oil refining infrastructure have been a major factor in supply disruptions, with Ukraine's Ministry of Defence claiming more than half of Russia's oil refining capacity has been taken offline. Trump has publicly pressed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to cease attacks on Russian diesel refinery plants, telling reporters, 'That's what's driving it up,' and warning Ukraine it 'has got to stop.'

Zelenskyy has rejected the characterization that he agreed to halt strikes on Russian energy assets, telling CBS News he would only stop targeting oil and gas infrastructure if Russia agreed to equivalent terms. The Kremlin, meanwhile, has intensified strikes on Ukrainian cities and critical infrastructure throughout the summer and fall. The announcement arrives one week after G7 nations agreed to release 100 million barrels of strategic reserves under White House pressure, and just weeks before the November 3 congressional elections that will determine control of Congress, lending the fuel price issue immediate domestic political significance.
